messages:
alex: FYI: starting to see a batch of GPU training jobs hang in eu-west pods. gRPC streams to model-server keep open but no tokens emitted for ~30s.
priya: Which pods and node pairs? east-west or same-node?
alex: Pod A (gpu-01) -> Pod B (model-serve-02) across nodes in same AZ. Not cross-AZ.
sam: Any network errors in kube-proxy or CNI logs? packet drops?
alex: grabbing tcpdump on node B, here's a snippet:```
17:45:12.123456 IP 10.8.3.22.56712 > 10.8.4.18.9000: Flags [P.], seq 2345:5432, ack 9876, win 65535
17:45:12.123789 IP 10.8.3.22 > 10.8.4.18: frag (id 54321, offset 0, more fragments)
17:45:12.124000 IP 10.8.3.22 > 10.8.4.18: frag (id 54321, offset 1480, more fragments)
``` 
alex: Notice repeated fragments but receiver never assembles; gRPC keeps waiting on reassembly.
maya: Do we have MTU mismatches on vtep or host interfaces? VXLAN sometimes forced 1450 vs host 9000.
priya: ran `ip link show` on both nodes: host has mtu 9000, veth for pod has mtu 1450 on node B.
sam: can you paste `ip route get` or `ip -s link`?
alex: `ip -s link show veth1234` shows lots of tx_errors=0 rx_errors=0 but `cat /proc/net/frag6` not helpful.
alex: On node A the kernel dropped fragments due to inability to allocate reassembly slab: kernel log snippet: ``[12789.543210] ip_frag_queue: reassembly timeout for id 54321 proto 17 from 10.8.3.22``
priya: That points to PMTU being clamped somewhere and GSO/GRO offload mismatch. Have we recently toggled offloads on NICs?
maya: We rolled a driver update last night on the Azure GPU nodes; ethtool shows `gso: on, gro: on` but `rxvlan: off` on host in some nodes.
sam: Also saw RDMA path fallback messages in the mlx driver logs: `mlx5_core: PMTU decrease event` on node B.
alex: Hypothesis: encapsulation + host mtu 9000 + vxlan mtu 1450 on veth -> large segmented packets get GSOed then forwarded into a path with smaller MTU and fragments not reassembled before gRPC streaming window.
priya: Quick mitigation: disable GSO on pod veths for the model server to avoid fragmented UDP/UDP-GSO, or bump VXLAN MTU to accommodate GPU message sizes.
maya: Can we try a canary: set `ethtool -K veth1234 gso off gro off` on node B for that pod and restart the model container.
alex: Doing that now. Patch command: `kubectl debug node/node-b -- sh -c "nsenter -t $(pgrep -f kube-proxy) -n -- ethtool -K veth1234 gso off gro off"` (adapted)
infra-bot: Deploy job 8423 started: canary gso-disable on 1 pod in eu-west-1.
alex: After disabling GSO the stream resumed immediately and tokens flowed. Latency dropped from 2-3s stalls to <50ms.
sam: Great validation. Long term we should audit PMTU discovery across the VXLAN overlay and driver updates. Also capture which nodes have mismatched offload defaults.
priya: I'll open a ticket to run a cluster-wide scan and create a remediation playbook: either enforce consistent MTU/VXLAN MTU or disable GSO for pods doing large gRPC frames.
maya: Also add a monitoring alert to trace `ip_fragmentation_reassembly_*` kernel counters and RDMA PMTU change events.
alex: I'll add logs from the canary and the exact ethtool diffs into the ticket. For now marking affected jobs as resumed. :white_check_mark:
priya: Thanks team — moving to postmortem if this repeats."
